risk_factors.title: Up to $900 Billion in Compute & Data Center Commitments
risk_factors.description: We have entered into $450B+ in non-cancelable cloud minimums ($111B Google, $110B AWS, $31B Microsoft) and up to $900B in total 10-year infrastructure pipeline commitments. Any slowdown in AI demand or pricing power could severely strain cash flows.

risk_factors.title: Pentagon 'Supply Chain Risk' Designation & Federal Ban
risk_factors.description: Following our refusal to remove acceptable-use prohibitions against mass domestic surveillance and autonomous lethal weapons, the U.S. Department of Defense designated Anthropic a 'supply chain risk' in 2026, barring defense contractors from using Claude while federal litigation proceeds.

risk_factors.title: Novel Multi-Class Governance & Public Benefit Mandate
risk_factors.description: Public Class A stockholders are capped at 49.9% voting power, Founder LLC holds 50.1% via Class F, and the Long-Term Benefit Trust appoints 4 of 7 directors via Class T. Our board may prioritize AI safety over short-term pecuniary returns, including pausing frontier models.

risk_factors.title: Copyright Litigation & Model Retraining Exposure
risk_factors.description: Following our historic $1.5B Bartz v. Anthropic book-author settlement (approved July 2026), we face ongoing multi-billion-dollar lawsuits from music publishers (Concord I & II, UMG, Sony). An adverse ruling could force us to pay heavy damages or retrain foundational models from scratch.

risk_factors.title: Hyperscaler Dual-Role Dependency (Suppliers & Competitors)
risk_factors.description: Amazon, Google, and Microsoft are simultaneously our largest compute suppliers, primary cloud distribution channels (~48% of H1 2026 revenue), major Class N stockholders, and direct competitors building rival frontier models.

risk_factors.title: Intense Frontier Model & Open-Weight Competition
risk_factors.description: We compete against heavily capitalized labs (OpenAI, Google DeepMind, Meta, xAI) that may bundle AI into dominant OS/cloud ecosystems or release open-weight models that compress per-token inference margins.

latest_news.title: Anthropic Prices Upsized $81.34B IPO at $83.00/Share ($1.5T FDV) — Largest IPO in History
latest_news.summary: Anthropic priced 980M Class A shares at $83.00/sh (above the $70–$78 range, upsized from 825M shares) plus a $26B concurrent Class N private placement (Google $10B, Nvidia $10B, AMD $2.5B, Broadcom/Micron/Microsoft $1B ea., TSMC $0.5B) for $107.34B in total gross proceeds ahead of Nov 19 Nasdaq: ANT trading.

latest_news.title: Anthropic Launches IPO Roadshow at $70–$78/Share ($1.4T Initial Target)
latest_news.summary: Amended Form S-1/A launched institutional bookbuilding for 825M Class A shares under Nasdaq ticker ANT alongside the $26B strategic Class N private placement before massive oversubscription drove the Nov 18 upsize to 980M shares at $83.00.

latest_news.title: Claude 5.5 Family, Mythos 5.2 & Fable 5.2 Debut Ahead of Public Listing
latest_news.summary: Anthropic rolls out Claude Opus 5.5, Sonnet 5.5, and Haiku 5.5 with 1M-token context windows, alongside specialized Mythos 5.2 (cybersecurity & CVE discovery) and Fable 5.2 models, plus desktop agent Claude Cowork.

latest_news.title: Public S-1 Reveals $33.2B 9M 2026 Revenue, $81B ARR & First Profitable Quarter
latest_news.summary: Public registration statement discloses Q2 2026 operating income of $974M, Q3 2026 revenue of ~$17.0B, $131.7B in liquid cash reserves, and up to $900B in 10-year compute commitments.

latest_news.title: Summary Judgment Argued in Concord & UMG Music Publisher Lawsuits
latest_news.summary: Judge Rita Lin hears summary judgment arguments in Concord I & II over song lyrics outputs and shadow-library training datasets, following the July 20, 2026 final court approval of the $1.5B Bartz v. Anthropic book settlement.

latest_news.title: Court Grants Final Approval to Historic $1.5B Bartz v. Anthropic Settlement
latest_news.summary: Judge Araceli Martínez-Olguín enters final judgment approving the largest copyright settlement in U.S. history (~$3,000 per work across ~500,000 books), resolving past shadow-library input claims with >91% claimant participation.

quotes.author: Dario & Daniela Amodei
quotes.text: There are four things that we would like any investor in Anthropic to understand: the incredible potential of AI, the risks we must address, Anthropic's unique approach to building a company, and the ways in which our behavior may differ from that of a purely profit-maximizing company.

quotes.author: Dario Amodei
quotes.text: We believe that AI is one of the most consequential technologies in human history—scaling toward what we describe as 'a country of geniuses in a data center' capable of compressing a century of biological and scientific discovery into a decade.

quotes.author: Anthropic PBC Charter
quotes.text: The specific public benefit to be promoted by the corporation is to responsibly develop and maintain advanced artificial intelligence for the long-term benefit of humanity.
